item.title: A train travel agency is used to practise basic maths in secondary school
item.description: Felip Sarroca has used Claude Code to create a game-style activity for mixed-ability groups in secondary school (ESO) and shares the code and a guide for adapting it.

media:content.media:description: A train follows a track; a ticket points to “Timetables and prices”. The track is closed (“Track closed”, marked with a red cross) and a blue detour, “Another route”, leads to the “Destination”. Labels: Timetables and prices, Another route, Track closed, Destination.

item.title: Elemental Cómics presents the periodic table with a comic for each element, according to its author
item.description: An interactive periodic table that, according to its author, opens each element as a comic followed by comprehension activities. It was created by Ernest Boixader and is shared under an open licence.

media:content.media:description: A colourful periodic table on a dark background, with the title “Elemental Cómics”, filter buttons for the families and the first rows of elements.

item.title: The conversation continued in Vibe Coding Educativo about whether it is better to program with AI agents…
item.description: The conversation continued in Vibe Coding Educativo about whether it is better to program with AI agents from the console or from the desktop app. One view held that the power is the same and the difference lies in autonomy: tasks that run on their own, without anyone requesting them; another replied that you can also automate from the app, in the cloud or with a computer left on, although it was admitted that for more advanced use of agents the console seems the better option. It was covered in the article Console or app: teachers compare how to work with a programming agent.

item.title: Vibe Coding Responsable 4.0: anything published openly must be reusable
item.description: Version 4.0 of Juan José de Haro’s guide explains that the educational exception in copyright law does not cover what is published on an open website.

media:content.media:description: Two shelves of images. On the left, a closed shelf with a padlock labelled “Closed classroom”. On the right, an open shelf with a verification badge labelled “Known licence”. Between them, an arrow labelled “Open”.

item.title: Transcribe audio and video and create subtitles without the file leaving your computer
item.description: Transcribe turns recordings into text and subtitles with the Whisper model, inside the browser and without sending anything to third parties. It was created by Juan José de Haro.

media:content.media:description: The Transcribe page with buttons to select audio or video and to import SRT or VTT files, the Whisper model selector, the transcription status and the box for the extracted text.

item.title: The ja.cat link shortener failed to load on the morning of Wednesday 25th and, according to a comment in…
item.description: The ja.cat link shortener failed to load on the morning of Wednesday 25th and, according to a comment in the group, the cause was an incident at its DNS provider, Dinahosting. A temporary workaround was suggested in the group, but it only works on the computer where it is applied.

item.title: Mis Gastos logs spending by category and charts it; it is used in History
item.description: Luis Villanueva Aizcorbe created “Mis Gastos”, a Spanish-language web app for logging expenses by category and viewing daily, monthly and yearly totals. According to its author, he uses it in his History classes.

media:content.media:description: The “Mis Gastos” app: a blue and green header with the motto “Controla tu dinero y vivirás mejor”, four totals at zero euros and the form with date, category, amount and description.

item.title: According to what was explained in the Vibe Coding Educativo group, the privacy guide that uses a traffic…
item.description: According to what was explained in the Vibe Coding Educativo group, the privacy guide that uses a traffic light to classify the tools analysed by the INTEF (Spain’s National Institute of Educational Technologies and Teacher Training) no longer shows the apps from the group’s repository, because that information is now in the repository itself. Background: the guide, published as a website with search.

item.title: The INTEF’s privacy guidelines move from a PDF to a website with search and filters
item.description: The guide uses a traffic-light system to classify the 1,144 tools analysed by the INTEF.

media:content.media:description: A traffic light with three lights: the red one, labelled “Do not use”; the amber one, labelled “With school permission”; and the green one, labelled “Can be used”. On the right, a list with a magnifying glass and the label “1,144 tools”.

item.title: A comparison tool helps you choose which free chatbot suits your needs
item.description: Juan José de Haro created a web app where you rate the importance of each feature and get a personalised ranking of free chatbots.

media:content.media:description: Two columns: on the left, sliders for the importance of each feature; on the right, the ranking of chatbots with percentages, led by Qwen on 91%.

item.title: An app turns spoken answers into assessment reports for families
item.description: “Informes a viva voz”, by Ernesto Boixader, asks teachers to answer three or seven questions about each student, and AI writes the report from those answers.

media:content.media:description: A microphone labelled “Voice”, with the label “3 or 7 questions”, an arrow to a robot labelled “AI writes” and another to a document labelled “Report”; below, a person with the label “Teacher reviews”.

item.title: An editor that turns ABC notation into a score and plays it in the browser
item.description: María Teresa González created a simple music editor: you type the melody as text, the score appears and you can listen to it, with nothing to install.

media:content.media:description: Editor with a text box in ABC notation on the left and, on the right, the audio controls and the score of a C major scale.

item.title: Google offered Opal for building apps without coding; a year later it has shut it down
item.description: In November 2025, Google offered Opal for free, a tool for building apps with AI without knowing how to code. It shut it down on 17 November 2026, and what people made with it does not move to Gemini on its own.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, an app window labelled “Opal”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same window crossed out with a red cross and labelled “Closed”, and a blue arrow pointing to a forward-slash icon labelled “Skills”.

item.title: Android lets you share your own app with up to 50 devices without Google Play
item.description: The limited distribution account is free and is intended for people who build apps for a class or a small group.

media:content.media:description: A QR code, labelled “QR code”, with an arrow towards a grid of phones followed by an ellipsis and the label “Up to 50 devices”; below, a red cross and the label “No Google Play”.

item.title: A simulator lets you build Rube Goldberg machines and analyse their levers
item.description: Students place pieces on a board, set the chain going and check the fulcrum, load and force of each simple machine. It is in Catalan.

media:content.media:description: A lever on a triangular fulcrum, labelled “Fulcrum”; on the left, a red downward arrow labelled “Force”, and on the right, a block on the lever labelled “Load”.

item.title: A Catalan-language train puzzle for planning shunting moves is new in the repository
item.description: The Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository adds eight resources in the week ending 20 November: one is presented here and seven have already had their own article.

media:content.media:description: Welcome screen of the game over a track layout with colourful numbered wagons, with a field for typing a player name.

item.title: Trama adds readings grouped into “universes” and versions of different difficulty
item.description: The reading-comprehension catalogue lets you choose readings that share the same world and versions of the same text at different levels. Its author asks for help translating it into Galician, Basque and Aranese.

media:content.media:description: On the left, three open books inside a dotted circle, “Universe”; on the right, three stacked sheets with lines of text of different lengths, “Variants”.

item.title: Google AI Studio builds complete Android apps from a description
item.description: It generates Kotlin apps with sign-in and a database, tests them in an in-browser emulator and lets you install them from your personal Google Play library.

media:content.media:description: A speech bubble labelled “Description” leads, with an arrow, to a browser window with a phone inside, labelled “Emulator”, and from there, with another arrow, to a box with a play symbol, labelled “Google Play”.

item.title: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper introduced on 12 November, now has “Laboratorio XR: Ensayo…
item.description: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper introduced on 12 November, now has “Laboratorio XR: Ensayo a la llama” (an XR flame-test lab) and a simulation of the human eye online. The page does not explain the lab’s requirements or say who makes it.

item.title: A teacher measures the use of their apps with Umami, cookie-free statistics
item.description: This tool shows which features students use without collecting names or email addresses.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: an app window with a pointer clicking sends its usage to a dashboard with a crossed-out eye; beside it, a cookie crossed out in red and a flag. Labels: App, Umami, No cookies, Error flag.

item.title: Antigravity buckled under demand at its free launch; a year on, it has paid plans
item.description: In November 2025, Google’s agent-based coding environment launched, free and overwhelmed. A year later it is on version 2.32, and extra usage requires a subscription.

media:content.media:description: Diptych with two identical windows. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a window with a warning triangle and the label “Overloaded”. On the right, “Today”: the same window with a blue padlock and the labels “Weekly limits” and “Pro and Ultra”.

item.title: Trama now has 245 reading texts in Catalan and Spanish, from the third year of primary school to the first…
item.description: Trama now has 245 reading texts in Catalan and Spanish, from the third year of primary school to the first year of ESO, according to its own website.

item.title: Three apps in Catalan: a classroom auction and two density labs
item.description: Felip Sarroca i Gil shares Subhasta, for working on scarcity and budgeting, and Densitats and Densitat, for studying flotation with Archimedes’ principle.

media:content.media:description: On the left, an auctioneer’s gavel on its block, with coins, labelled “Auction”. On the right, a tank of water in which a block floats, with an upward arrow labelled “Buoyancy” and the label “Flotation”.

item.title: Agente Clima IES analyses classroom temperature and humidity in the browser
item.description: The app reads sensor logs and compares them with the limits set by the regulation on workplaces.

media:content.media:description: A document labelled “CSV” passes into a browser window, labelled “In the browser”, containing a thermometer with the label “17–27 °C” and water drops with the label “30–70%”.

item.title: A robotic palletising cell is simulated in the browser and exports the scene as .glb
item.description: According to the message of the person who shared it, the app was built with AI models; it lets users stop, resume and monitor a virtual industrial cell and export the scene for Blender.

media:content.media:description: Diagram from left to right: a browser window with a robotic cell (conveyor with boxes, robot arm and pallet) and a vertical red line marking the safety curtain; a blue arrow towards a 3D cube. Labels: “Cell in the browser”, “Light curtain”, “.glb” and “Blender”.

item.title: Trama offers 206 reading texts with questions for building reading comprehension worksheets
item.description: The catalogue, in Catalan and Spanish, is aimed mainly at the fourth to sixth years of primary school and lets teachers choose the questions before printing the worksheet or downloading it as a PDF.

media:content.media:description: Trama's catalogue of reading texts with filters on the left and cards showing an illustration, title, school year, difficulty and a “Prepara la fitxa” button.

item.title: Chrome publishes Modern Web Guidance 1.0, a guide to the current web for coding agents
item.description: The guide brings together expert-verified solutions and compatibility data to correct the outdated knowledge of models.

media:content.media:description: Three boxes joined by arrows: a file with a clock, labelled “Old data”, an open book guide, labelled “Current web guide”, and a code file with a red tick, labelled “Current code”.

item.title: Battleships in Catalan, against the machine or online with a room code
item.description: “Enfonsar la flota” is a web version of the classic battleships game, with a 10×10 board, which works on coordinates and strategy in primary and secondary school.

media:content.media:description: Start screen of the game with two cards: “Partida en línia”, with a button to create a room and a code field, and “Contra la màquina”, with three difficulty levels.

item.title: Antigravity adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and an Orchestrator mode that shares out the work
item.description: Orchestrator combines Hydrogen with more powerful models; access depends on Google’s paid plan.

media:content.media:description: Under the title “Orchestrator”, two boxes: on the left one with a branching diagram, labelled “Carbon plans”, and on the right one with a code file, labelled “Hydrogen edits”. An arrow carries the work from the first to the second and a red arrow goes back, labelled “If it gets stuck”.

item.title: A teacher asks Codex to model Industrial Revolution machines in Blender
item.description: Felip Sarroca i Gil says his computer cannot open Blender, but Codex can operate it, and it has generated 3D models for his website for fourth-year ESO students.

media:content.media:description: A diagram from left to right: a speech bubble labelled “Request” leads to a cog labelled “Codex + Blender”, which leads to a cube with three dots labelled “3D model”; a curved red arrow, labelled “More realism”, returns from the model to the request.

item.title: GeoBreath guides breathing exercises with geometric shapes and an adjustable rhythm
item.description: Luis Vilela Acuña's app uses an animated shape to show when to breathe in, hold and breathe out. It opens in the browser, with nothing to install, and is available in six languages.

media:content.media:description: GeoBreath screen with a square along whose sides a dot travels, the prompt “Inspira” in the centre, the session and cycle counters and the selector for shape and seconds per side.

item.title: A web editor lets teachers design collectable fauna and flora cards for the classroom
item.description: The Eco-Duel Card Generator, created by David Cordones, offers a form for composing cards with data on animals and plants, with one collection per school year, from the first year of primary to the second year of Bachillerato.

media:content.media:description: Card editor with the form on the left and, on the right, a fauna card called Senglar with size 7, level 3 and speed 5, and the buttons Descarregar and Copiar above it.

item.title: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper presented on 12 November, has a 3D simulation for…
item.description: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper presented on 12 November, has a 3D simulation for preparing a NaOH solution and measuring the acidity of vinegar, according to its description.

item.title: Conservatoire regulations, indicators and classroom games, new in the repository
item.description: The Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository adds 25 resources this week: 13 are presented here and 12 have already had their own article.

media:content.media:description: Home page of the Legis CPMDEM catalogue with a search box, filters for validity and categories of regulation, and the first entries for decrees and orders.

item.title: Atlas en xogo, a map game in Galician, joins EDUmind’s apps
item.description: A new interactive geography app in Galician has been shared in Vibe Coding Educativo. A full description of its game modes could not be checked.

media:content.media:description: A browser window with a map and the label “Atlas en xogo”; to its left, a magnifying glass with a plus sign, labelled “Zoom”; to its right, a globe labelled “3D view”.

item.title: Relleu Obert turns a piece of real map into a 3D model that can be printed for the classroom
item.description: A free, open-source project lets you pick a place, generate its relief in the browser and export it for 3D printing.

media:content.media:description: Three steps joined by arrows: a map labelled “Map”, a mountain labelled “Relief” and a printer labelled “Model”.

item.title: A tool helps apply the order of priority in admissions to Valencian conservatoires
item.description: José Luis Miralles Bono has created a website with diagrams, an age calculator and Excel templates for applying Order 8/2026 in music and dance schools in the Valencian Community.

media:content.media:description: Page titled “Prelación de acceso a conservatorio”, with a tab bar (Outline, Timeline, Step-by-step guide, Age, Reorientation, Definitions, Templates) and four collapsible blocks of allocations.

item.title: A Catalan-language website tells the story of the spice trade from Marco Polo onwards with maps, games and questions
item.description: “El comerç de les espècies” offers nine interactive chapters, designed, according to its author, for secondary school and sixth-form students.

media:content.media:description: A route with nine points running from a ship, labelled “Marco Polo”, to a globe, labelled “Today”; above, the label “Nine chapters”.

item.title: Terminal or app: teachers compare ways of working with a coding agent
item.description: The group discussed whether the terminal offers more freedom than the graphical app, and concluded that it depends on the person and the task.

media:content.media:description: Three icons labelled “Web”, “App” and “Terminal” whose lines converge on a single box labelled “Result”.

item.title: Reloj EDUmind brings together timers for the classroom, group work and independent study
item.description: Luis has created an installable web app with three timer modes, designed for managing time in class from nursery to vocational training.

item.title: Anthropic advises that, to keep Fable 5.2 responsible for an action, you should write “ask for approval…
item.description: Anthropic advises that, to keep Fable 5.2 responsible for an action, you should write “ask for approval before deleting files” instead of “never delete files”, and reply with the specific instruction rather than a simple “go ahead”. It follows the guide the paper reported on.

item.title: The author of the school music bell has published their project on GitHub: an installation guide, a manual…
item.description: The author of the school music bell has published their project on GitHub: an installation guide, a manual for the staff and the code, with an AGPL licence for the code and CC BY-SA 4.0 for the documentation.

item.title: Anthropic recommends telling Fable 5.2 the code is its own if you want it to reorganise it
item.description: Anthropic's guide to Fable 5.2 explains that the model behaves differently depending on who is named as the owner of the code, at a cost in tokens.

media:content.media:description: Two columns: on the left, two identical blocks of code and the labels “Adds” and “Under 10%”; on the right, a merge icon above a single block of code and the labels “Merges” and “75%”.

item.title: Eduvers brings together interactive Physics and Chemistry simulations and is preparing 3D virtual labs
item.description: Its author is adding simulations to the website and announces that he will link 3D labs in the coming weeks.

media:content.media:description: Three cards under the label “Simulations and labs”: the parabolic trajectory of a ball, “Physics”; a flask, “Chemistry”; and a 3D cube, “3D lab”.

item.title: A music-class app asks students to place the notes of a score on the stave
item.description: Pentagrama Maestro, created by Iñaki Fernández, plays note by note and offers three levels and unlimited games.

media:content.media:description: A stave with four rising notes, labelled “Stave”, and an arrow leading to a loudspeaker labelled “Listen”; below, three bars of increasing height labelled “3 levels”.

item.title: Tribunator organises panels, rooms and timetables for a conservatoire's entrance exams
item.description: José Luis Miralles Bono has created, with the help of Claude, a tool that plans who sits on each panel, in which room and at what time they examine, and checks for clashes before anything is published.

media:content.media:description: Tribunator welcome screen with the tabs Home, Space, Time, Templates, Panels and Verification, and the buttons Start from scratch, Import data and Load example.

item.title: Anthropic is giving plans that include Fable between one and three usage-limit resets, depending on the…
item.description: Anthropic is giving plans that include Fable between one and three usage-limit resets, depending on the length of the subscription, which can be used until 8 March 2027; Pro gets one, only until 16 November. The model is Fable 5.2.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, the latter only for verified organisations
item.description: The company announces two versions of the same model: Fable 5.2, with safeguards and no prior verification, and Mythos 5.2, only for verified organisations.

media:content.media:description: A diagram of a trunk, “Claude 5.2”, that forks into two branches: “Fable 5.2”, which leads to a group of people labelled “No verification”, and “Mythos 5.2”, which leads to a padlocked closed door labelled “Verified”.

item.title: Two Catalan-language apps by David Cordones: a letters and numbers game and a reception classroom
item.description: Xifres i Lletres trains vocabulary and mental arithmetic by age; Aula d'Acollida Digital offers initial language support.

media:content.media:description: Two panels: on the left, a calculator and three boxes labelled “Xifres i Lletres”; on the right, a translation icon labelled “Aula d'Acollida”; below, a dashed box labelled “Open source”.

item.title: A website promotes Belsetán, an endangered Aragonese variety, with games and classroom worksheets
item.description: “El aprendiz del pastor” brings together history, texts, games and teaching materials on the language of the Bielsa valley.

media:content.media:description: A mountain labelled “Bielsa Valley” leads to an open book labelled “Belsetán”, from which two arrows come out: one to a pair of dice labelled “Games” and another to a document labelled “Worksheets”.
